about: Something changed by a calling's own skill (a lock picked, a door forced, an old hand read, a dead man laid to rest, a broken thing mended, a wall climbed): told as the act it is, in a sentence of how it went, before what it came to. Picking takes care and an eye on the way back; forcing is loud. The blind playtest of 13 November: a thief's padlock had only 'hung open on its hasp'.

lines.text: You work a bent pin and a thin blade into the lock and feel for its wards one at a time, with an ear to the way you came, until the last of them gives.
It is an old lock and a stiff one. You take your time over it, by feel, and it turns at last with a sound like a knuckle cracking.
The wards are crude and the spring is tired; it takes a pin, a breath held, and a quarter-turn more than it should.
You set your shoulder to it and heave. Wood groans and iron shrieks, and the noise of it goes further than you would like.
It holds, and holds, and then it does not, all at once, with a crack that anyone near will have heard.
The letters are worn shallow, but they are letters you have met before in older books; you read them slowly, under your breath, and they hold together.
It takes a while, and a finger along each line, but the old hand is one you were taught, and it gives up its sense.
You go up it by the cracks and the old fixings, testing each before you trust it with your weight.
You say the words for the dead as they were said over your own, without hurrying, and the place is quieter when you have done.
You work at it with what you have, patiently, as you were taught, until it holds.
You do not argue. You let them talk, agree with the half of it that is true, and the rest comes round of itself.
